key_insight: Partial quantum error correction can turn fault-tolerant error-correction cycles into a programmable source of controlled logical dissipation instead of only suppressing noise.
engineering_relevance: This provides a resource-efficient way to compile target open-system dynamics directly at the logical level without introducing explicit bath ancilla qubits.
method: Run one fault-tolerant error-correction round to induce a logical CPTP map.
Randomize decoder/recovery choices to generate a controllable family of logical channels.
Mix these channels convexly to realize target Kraus-channel dissipators and set code distance so residual logical errors stay below the intended dissipation per step.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a theoretical derivation of an accuracy criterion for multi-step simulation and a compilation framework for target dissipators, rather than a numerical benchmark.
watch_item: Practical performance still depends on choosing a code distance that keeps unintended logical errors small relative to the desired dissipation, which may be challenging on noisy hardware.
paper_title: Programmable Dissipation via Partial Quantum Error Correction
